A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix K report original simulations comparing BC and MURMAIL in constructed and randomly generated Markov games, illustrated in Figures 2 and 4.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix J retain these original simulation results, including Figures 2 and 4.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same policy updates, uncertainty rewards, oracle calls, RL procedures, and optional BC initialization. The revised coverage coefficients and expanded general-sum derivation change the analysis rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven-state construction with varying expert coverage and the same random ten-state zero-sum game. No additional empirical tasks or environments appear.

E2.justification: BC remains the empirical comparator to MURMAIL in both environments. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparison methods, including Tang et al.'s BC, MALICE, and BLADES.

E3.justification: Appendix K in v1 and Appendix J in v2 specify identical action spaces, discount factor 0.9, expert mixtures, initial-state distributions, exploitability calculation, and learning-rate selection.

E4.justification: The coverage-sensitivity comparison in Figure 2 and random-game validation in Figure 4 are retained. Warm starts, sample reuse, and initial-dataset initialization remain the same practical discussion rather than newly evaluated ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging 1,000 runs with different seeds. The plotted shaded bands are unchanged, with no added uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 4 preserve the same curves and shaded regions after resizing, together with the same BC-versus-MURMAIL findings. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or numerically revised; theoretical bound revisions are covered under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 replaces the recovered-policy-dependent coefficient with C_max, maximizing over policies and both players' coverage ratios. Appendix C adds the corresponding argument and a general sampling-distribution formulation; Table 1 changes the BC sample bound to depend on C_max squared. Appendix H expands the general-sum proof substantially and replaces explicit n-squared bounds with unspecified polynomial dependence.

C1.justification: The abstract and central BC contribution now concern an all-policy coverage coefficient rather than the earlier single-policy coefficient. The conclusion distinguishes this upper-bound quantity from the smaller expert-policy coefficient underlying the impossibility result. The two interactive algorithms' principal complexity claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 removes the claimed infinite-data identification of the recovered-policy and expert coefficients and the associated unique-best-response argument for favorable BC behavior. Sections 3 and 6 instead acknowledge an unresolved gap between the two coverage conditions and open questions about statistical lower bounds and BC optimality.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a repository link for the experimental code. The PDFs otherwise retain the same implementation and experimental details; the repository's contents or accessibility were not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds the specific comparison that Tang et al.'s BC bound is vacuous for the construction experiments with beta equal to zero. The cited works remain the same; several references receive publication updates rather than representing added literature.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 revises coefficient terminology, makes localized language corrections, moves existing future-direction discussions into Section 6, and removes the acknowledgments paragraph.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset in NeurIPS format, changing the title and author arrangement, body typography, margins, spacing, and placement and sizing of tables, figures, and algorithm boxes. The existing four figures and table structure are retained rather than replaced by new empirical displays.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the coverage gap, expands the general-sum analysis, and adds code-access information. However, Appendix C replaces a sum of coverage terms by their maximum while retaining the same bound constant without justification. The new Appendix H Eq. (18) also equates joint squared total variation with a sum of marginal squares, which independence does not justify. These proof issues leave the net quality effect uncertain despite improved transparency.
